chapters.title: Confront Your Dark Side: The Law of Repression

chapterBreakdown.gentle: The chapter on repression stays useful because it names a pattern people often feel before they can explain it. This law argues that people repress traits they dislike or fear in themselves, but those traits do not disappear. They leak out through projection, overreaction, moralizing, and contradiction. Because the material is still alive, it returns sideways. A person projects motives onto others, moralizes too hard, loses proportion under small provocations, or lives a contradictory life in which the forbidden trait keeps leaking through. The shadow is therefore readable through overcompensation and disproportion. The practical move is integration. Name the denied trait, see the energy inside it, and give it a conscious place before it has to emerge in disguised form. This does not make someone saintly. It makes them less split and less dangerous to themselves and others. Integration reduces hidden rule; it does not excuse acting out. That softer honesty is already a practical advantage.
